records.issue_text: [BUG] The h3 light branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%). Mobile light-theme users see linked-preview h3 titles at half the previous contrast; a light-theme regression outside the PR's stated scope.
records.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss`, the `a.star h3` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which makes the light-theme branch use 50% lightness instead of 20%. records.issue_text: [BUG] The light-theme branch of the colorspace was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), which is not the mechanical 100-L inversion the PR title promises. Light-theme users see the small-action links in post rows rendered at 70% lightness of $primary (near-white) instead of the previous darker 30% tone — a light-mode regression completely unrelated to the stated 'fix dark themes' intent; nobody asked for the light branch to change here.
records.rationale: The diff shows at least one place where the *light-theme* (first argument to `dark-light-choose`) was changed, not just wrapped. In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` the rule for a link changes from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`, which means light mode now uses 70% lightness instead of the previous 30%. That is a visible light-theme behavior change/regression and matches the finding’s mechanism.
